question: Does identity survive the persistence boundary, and do rounds 002-004's findings still hold after a save/reload cycle?
prediction_made_before_measuring: M1-M3 will hold; M4 will lose information because mapped names reference string IDs held by the hasher.
prediction_outcome: M1-M3 held. M4 was NOT REFUTED AND NOT CONFIRMED - it could not be exercised at this level, which the round records rather than scoring as a pass.

environment.level: TopoShape, via the real ElementMap::save/restore path

measurements.name: a stored reference resolves after reload
downstream naming is deterministic after a reload
measurements.why_it_matters: The same change applied to a reloaded shape produced byte-identical mapped names to the same change applied to a never-saved one. References captured before a save are therefore not at risk after one.

measurements.name: restore with a fresh hasher
measurements.reason: The shapes carried no StringHasher, so the save stored no string IDs and a fresh hasher was indistinguishable from the real one. The clean result means nothing.

measurements.name: M4 retried with a shared hasher and a five-deep boolean chain
measurements.reason: ElementMap::beforeSave only MARKS StringIDs already attached to mapped names; it does not create them. The names produced by this construction path carry none, so the string table stays empty.

measurements.name: negative control: the name comparison must detect a difference

compatibility_classification_52_5.save_restore_with_lost_string_table: UNCLASSIFIED - could not be exercised at TopoShape level

caveats: TopoShape-level persistence, not a document .FCStd round-trip. The latter is blocked by the material-library limitation recorded in round 002.
The string-table dependency is real in the code and unreachable from this level. It is the round's largest gap, not a resolved question.
One shape family (box with pockets), faces only.
